speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe exactly where in your neck the pain is located and whether it radiates down a specific arm? Also, have you noticed any weakness in your grip or difficulty lifting your arm?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do the paresthesias and weakness affect all fingers in both hands equally, or is it primarily the thumb, index, and middle fingers? Have you noticed any night-time symptoms that wake you up, or does shaking your hands provide relief?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of fasciculations, absent reflexes, and bilateral hand weakness is concerning for lower motor neuron involvement. I need to rule out cervical myelopathy or radiculopathy given your neck pain and accident history. REQUEST TEST: MRI of the Cervical Spine

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI confirms a syrinx, which explains your burning pain, paresthesias, and lower motor neuron signs like fasciculations and absent reflexes. To investigate the underlying cause, particularly given your history of trauma, I need to look for associated structural abnormalities. REQUEST TEST: MRI of the Brain and Craniovertebral Junction

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal brain MRI rules out Chiari malformation, suggesting the syrinx may be post-traumatic from your previous accident. I need to assess the extent of the neurological deficit to determine if surgical intervention is necessary. REQUEST TEST: Electromyography and Nerve Conduction Studies

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal EMG and NCS results are unexpected given the clinical signs of weakness and fasciculations, suggesting the pathology is central rather than peripheral. Given the confirmed cervical syrinx and history of trauma, the diagnosis is post-traumatic syringomyelia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-traumatic Syringomyelia
